title: The GenAI Boom Accelerates And Transforms Ethernet Switching
gist: IDC data for Q2 2026 shows Ethernet switch revenue up 43.4 percent to $18.91 billion, with datacenter switching up 64.5 percent to $12.3 billion and 800Gb/sec switch revenue up 6.1X to $5.07 billion; Nvidia grew Ethernet sales 2.8X to $3.86 billion on Spectrum-X attach to its GenAI systems, while component shortages and price hikes cap how fast the market can grow.

insights.claim: Ethernet switch revenues rose 43.4 percent year on year to $18.91 billion in Q2 2026, and were also up 23.1 percent sequentially from Q1 2026 — record sales for the category.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 23 percent sequential jump in a normally slow-moving infrastructure market signals the networking leg of the AI capex cycle has finally turned.
insights.quote: switch revenues rose by 43.4 percent to $18.91 billion, which was also a 23.1 percent growth sequentially from switch sales Q1 2026
insights.locator: In the second quarter, which is the latest one

insights.claim: Switch demand is not only a datacenter GenAI story: edge and campus networks are being upgraded specifically to feed into GenAI systems, broadening the addressable spend beyond AI clusters.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Campus and edge networking vendors get an indirect AI tailwind that consensus models may be assigning only to datacenter switching.
insights.quote: it is not only because of GenAI systems in the datacenters, but because edge and campus networks have to be upgraded to feed into GenAI systems
insights.locator: So let's be clear: This is record sales

insights.claim: The router market, under structural pressure for over a decade as routing functions migrate into Ethernet switch ASICs, still grew 22.8 percent to $4.51 billion and 20.1 percent sequentially because service providers, telcos and neoclouds cannot write their own switch routing software the way hyperscalers do.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A secularly declining router franchise is getting a cyclical reprieve — a possible upside surprise at Cisco, Nokia and Ericsson that bears have written off.
insights.locator: The router market, which has been under pressure

insights.claim: Component shortages are the binding constraint on switch market growth, but demand outstripping supply is itself lifting revenue through price increases, so the shortage partly pays for itself in reported growth.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Networking revenue growth is flattered by price, not just units — check unit and port data before extrapolating vendor top lines.
insights.quote: It probably won't be able to grow as fast as it might because of component shortages, but then again, demand outstripping supply and creating its own kind of rise thanks to price increases.
insights.locator: The server market is exploding thanks to the GenAI boom

insights.claim: Semiconductor pricing power is described as effectively arbitrary right now — vendors can cross out an old price and write a higher one with no customer recourse.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Gross-margin expansion across the chip and networking supply chain may be a pricing artifact that reverses when supply normalizes.
insights.quote: You can just get a red grease pencil and scratch out an old price and write down a newer high price because you feel like it. What is anyone gonna do about it?
insights.locator: It is a good time to be pricing out any kind of semiconductor

insights.claim: Even with component shortages, cost per 800Gb/sec port is coming down because hyperscalers and cloud builders negotiate hard for discounts and vendors make it up in volume.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Buyer concentration is capping ASP gains at the top end — volume, not price, drives the 800G revenue line.
insights.locator: There is a huge wave of adoption for 800 Gb/sec

themes.theme: Vendor scoreboard and Nvidia's networking land grab

insights.claim: Nvidia's Ethernet revenues grew 2.8X year on year to $3.86 billion in Q2 2026 on Spectrum-X attach to DGX server nodes and NVL72 rackscale systems, dwarfing Arista Networks' $2.53 billion.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia has become a top-two Ethernet vendor in under two years purely as an attach to its own systems — direct share loss risk for Arista and Cisco.
insights.quote: Nvidia grew by 2.8X thanks to its enormous GenAI systems business and its attachment rate for its Spectrum-X switches
insights.locator: Cisco's overall Ethernet revenues grew by 36.2 percent

insights.claim: Cisco's overall Ethernet revenues grew 36.2 percent to $5.43 billion in Q2 2026 and its datacenter Ethernet sales grew 77.3 percent to $2.24 billion, a figure that excludes Silicon One ASIC revenue sold to hyperscalers who have ODMs build their own switches.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Cisco's reported datacenter switch share understates its true AI networking exposure because merchant Silicon One sales sit outside the IDC switch line.
insights.locator: Cisco grew datacenter Ethernet sales by a very good 77.3 percent

insights.claim: Arista Networks grew datacenter Ethernet 37.9 percent to $2.3 billion, remaining only marginally larger than Cisco in the datacenter segment and growing at roughly half Cisco's datacenter rate.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Arista's datacenter leadership over Cisco has narrowed to a rounding error — a share-narrative risk for the premium multiple.
insights.locator: Arista Networks is still marginally larger than Cisco

insights.claim: Hewlett Packard Enterprise's Ethernet switch business grew only 6.1 percent to $1.15 billion even after absorbing Juniper Networks, and its datacenter Ethernet was just $345 million despite growing 2.1X — under one-tenth of Nvidia's scale-out Ethernet take.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The Juniper acquisition has not yet bought HPE relevance in AI datacenter switching; the synergy case remains unproven.
insights.locator: Even after eating Juniper Networks

insights.claim: Huawei Technology edged past HPE in Ethernet switching with $1.55 billion in revenues, up 28.6 percent, after several years of the two jockeying for position.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Huawei continues to compound switch share despite sanctions, a reminder that non-US networking supply is not shrinking.
insights.locator: Huawei Technology has been jockeying with HPE

insights.claim: IDC no longer publishes a collective ODM figure, but the author's estimate puts ODM switch revenue at $3.56 billion, up 2.43X year on year, implying the remaining long-tail vendors have seen share collapse.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Whitebox switching is compounding faster than any branded vendor except Nvidia — a structural margin threat to tier-two networking names.
insights.quote: IDC is no longer providing figures for the collective original design manufacturers (ODMs), but I estimate they raked in $3.56 billion, up 2.43X year on year.
insights.locator: Huawei Technology has been jockeying with HPE

insights.claim: On the author's estimates Nvidia outgrew the entire ODM collective in scale-out datacenter Ethernet, and if the ODM estimate is too high the gap in Nvidia's favor is even wider.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Nvidia is taking AI networking share from whitebox as well as from branded incumbents — a stronger position than share tables suggest.
insights.locator: If my number for the ODM collective is right

insights.claim: Datacenter Ethernet switch revenues hit $12.3 billion in Q2 2026, up 64.5 percent year on year and 23 percent sequentially, representing 65.1 percent of total switch revenue but only 42.8 percent of ports shipped.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Datacenter ports carry roughly 2.5x the revenue intensity of campus ports — mix shift alone lifts blended vendor ASPs.
insights.locator: In Q2, datacenter Ethernet switch revenues totaled $12.3 billion

insights.claim: An estimated 129.5 million datacenter switch ports were sold in Q2 2026 across scale-up, scale-out and scale-across networks, and mostly for scale-out — a balance the author expects to change.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A coming shift from scale-out toward scale-up networking would reshuffle which switch ASIC and protocol vendors win the next tranche of ports.
insights.quote: I reckon that around 129.5 million ports were sold into the datacenter market for scale up, scale out, and scale across networks – and mostly for scale out. (This will change.)
insights.locator: In Q2, datacenter Ethernet switch revenues totaled $12.3 billion

insights.claim: Revenue from switches with 800Gb/sec ports rose 6.1X year on year to $5.07 billion and 41.5 percent sequentially, and those switches were sold exclusively for datacenter use cases.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: 800G is the single fastest-growing line item in networking and a pure-play read on AI cluster buildouts.
insights.locator: In the quarter, sales of switches with 800 Gb/sec ports

insights.claim: 800Gb/sec switches went from 35.9 percent of datacenter ports shipped in Q1 2026 to 41.2 percent in Q2 2026, with an estimated 35.3 million such ports in Q1 rising to 54.3 million in Q2.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A 54 percent sequential jump in 800G port volume is the demand signal for optics, DSP and retimer suppliers.
insights.locator: IDC gave us a hint that in the datacenter sector

insights.claim: Switches with 200Gb/sec or 400Gb/sec ports, sold almost exclusively into datacenters, grew 71.6 percent to $6.35 billion on an estimated 35.8 million ports, still out-earning the 800Gb/sec tier.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The 400G installed base is still the larger revenue pool, so a 400G-exposed supplier is not yet a melting ice cube.
insights.locator: Sales of Ethernet switches with 200 Gb/sec or 400 Gb/sec ports

insights.claim: Per-port prices for 800Gb/sec and 200/400Gb/sec switches came down only slightly, while switches are carrying more ports as 51.2Tb/sec and 102.4Tb/sec ASICs arrive, so higher radix and bandwidth are pushing switch revenue up per box.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Revenue per chassis is rising even as price per port falls — the ASIC bandwidth roadmap, not port pricing, is the revenue driver to model.
insights.locator: The prices per port for 800 Gb/sec or 200/400 Gb/sec switches

themes.theme: Next-gen interconnect and the NVLink challenge

insights.claim: 1.6Tb/sec switches are expected to ramp in volume for high-end GenAI systems before long, with low-latency Ethernet using UALink or ESUN protocols emerging as an alternative to Nvidia's NVLink/NVSwitch combination.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: An open Ethernet-based scale-up fabric is the key structural threat to Nvidia's captive interconnect margin — watch UALink and ESUN silicon tape-outs.
insights.quote: it won't be long before 1.6 Tb/sec switches are ramping in volume for high-end GenAI systems and low latency Ethernet with UALink or ESUN protocols becomes an alternative to Nvidia's NVLink/NVSwitch combo
insights.locator: The prices per port for 800 Gb/sec or 200/400 Gb/sec switches

insights.claim: IDC's Ethernet data excludes the high-speed scale-up networks inside GPU-laden rackscale systems, so published switch market figures systematically understate total AI networking spend.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Any AI networking TAM built off IDC switch revenue is missing the fastest-growing scale-up layer entirely.
insights.locator: The rapidly growing server market

insights.claim: In Q2 2026 roughly 6.2X more server cores were sold than switch ports running above 10Gb/sec, which the author reads as evidence that companies are not spending enough on networking to balance their compute.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: A persistent core-to-port ratio gap is a leading indicator that networking capex must catch up — supportive of a multi-year switch and optics upcycle.
insights.quote: It is not hard to conjecture that companies are not spending enough on networking to balance out their compute. This happens all the time, and people wonder why their server utilization is so low.
insights.locator: In Q2 2026, I estimate that there were 6.2X more server cores sold

insights.claim: The server market's GenAI-driven expansion is only now beginning to lift the switch market, implying networking demand lags server demand rather than moving with it.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: The lag means switch vendors' best comparables may be ahead of, not behind, the peak in server revenue growth.
insights.locator: The blue line is when IDC stopped giving out server revenues

insights.claim: IDC's public Ethernet switch dataset only goes back to Q3 2013, so the current GenAI boom cannot be compared against the Dot Com boom and bust or the Great Recession in the same series.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: No one has a comparable-cycle benchmark for this networking upturn — a reason to distrust confident mean-reversion calls in either direction.
insights.locator: The public IDC dataset for the Ethernet switch market

insights.claim: IDC stopped publishing datacenter and campus/edge switch port counts after Q2 2022 and stopped publishing server revenues in its public statements, leaving analysts reliant on modeled estimates for unit trends.
insights.speaker: Timothy Prickett Morgan
insights.so_what: Deteriorating public data quality raises the error bars on every networking unit forecast in circulation.
insights.locator: To be fair, IDC used to give out revenues and port counts
